senateStanding.note: One of the 13 United Methodist schools of theology.

onlineCredit.note: GBHEM: all United Methodist schools of theology are approved to provide a fully online M.Div. that meets the educational requirements for UM ordination.

coverage.note: ST 6303 Systematic Theology in the core.

No core course is labelled this way. MT 6300 Christian Ethics in Social Context is required, and the Division II and IV core electives include World Christianity (WX) and Christianity and Society (XS) options that plausibly satisfy it. Which course your board accepts is a question for your registrar — don't assume.
Evangelism (EV) is one of roughly eleven options for the single Division IV practical core elective, and is otherwise unrestricted elective space. Choosable, but not automatic.

Nothing in the required core covers United Methodist doctrine, polity, or history. The old degree plan states plainly that the 24 unrestricted elective hours “may include United Methodist Studies and Evangelism.” ¶324.4 asks for a minimum of 6 semester hours here.

ordination.gapSummary: Six of the nine ¶324.4 areas are in the required core and take care of themselves. Three are not. United Methodist studies — the 6-hour one — sits in elective space, as does evangelism, and no core course is labelled “mission of the church in the world.” This is the thing to notice about a Perkins M.Div.: it is a United Methodist seminary, but the United Methodist studies requirement is something you choose, not something the degree hands you. Plan the elective block around it in your first year rather than discovering the gap in year three.

gapRemedies.blurb: Build the 24 unrestricted elective hours around ¶324.4 from the start. Six hours of United Methodist studies, three of evangelism, and a course your board will accept for mission of the church — that is half the elective block, and it still leaves twelve hours free.
Perkins also offers the ¶324.4 studies on their own, outside a degree. The nondegree “Basic Graduate Theological Studies” track exists for UMC deacons and for anyone closing a gap.

Ask the Perkins registrar for the current M.Div. degree-progress sheet, and ask your conference's Board of Ordained Ministry registrar which specific course numbers they accept for each ¶324.4 area. They make the call, not the catalogue and not us.

tuitionPerCredit.note: Academic year 2026–27. D.Min. is $928 and D.P.M. $906. Fees are charged on top — see below.

fees.label: Community life fee
fees.amount: $25 per term, Dallas and hybrid students

typicalAward.note: For full-time, degree-seeking students. An average, not a floor — awards vary.

cost.honestNote: The sticker figure most people quote is tuition alone. Perkins charges a general student fee per credit hour on top of it, and hybrid students add two more. Ask for a full cost-of-attendance sheet, not a per-credit number — and note that applying for admission is also the scholarship application, so applying early matters: Perkins says its funds go first-come, first-served.

degrees.name: Master of Divinity
degrees.typicalYears: 3–7 years; all requirements within 7 calendar years of first registration
degrees.blurb: The ordination degree. 75 credit hours including a supervised internship, with 24 credit hours of elective space.

degrees.name: Maestría en Divinidad
degrees.blurb: The M.Div. taught in Spanish — fully in Spanish for the first two years, with the option to move to a bilingual track after that.

degrees.name: Master of Arts in Ministry
degrees.blurb: 36 credit hours plus an internship, for ministerial leadership that doesn't require the full M.Div.

degrees.name: Master of Theological Studies
degrees.blurb: 48 credit hours plus a thesis or summative project. Not an ordination degree — lay leadership, personal study, or groundwork for a PhD.

degrees.name: Master of Sacred Music
degrees.blurb: For church musicians; paired with a Doctor of Pastoral Music.

degrees.name: Basic Graduate Theological Studies (nondegree)
degrees.blurb: The ¶324.4 studies taken on their own, without enrolling in a degree. Built for UMC deacons and for anyone closing a gap.

partnerships.blurb: Perkins is a school within SMU, on the Dallas campus at 5905 Bishop Blvd.

Classes meet regularly in Houston at St. Paul's UMC, Houston Methodist Hospital, and St. John's UMC downtown; in Galveston at Moody Memorial First UMC. You can serve a Gulf Coast appointment and still take courses in person.

The in-person requirement for the M.Div. and M.A.M. can be met through week-long immersions held in Dallas, Houston–Galveston and elsewhere — recent ones in McAllen and Waco, Texas, and Memphis, Tennessee. Perkins says it adds locations based on where students actually live.
Perkins' own theological library, with special collections and the Center for World Methodism.

courseOfStudy.blurb: Perkins administers the United Methodist Regional Course of Study School — the five-year curriculum required of licensed local pastors who are not in a seminary degree program — in partnership with GBHEM. It runs in English and, as Curso de Estudio, in Spanish.
